output.summary: KEP-2451 proposed a ServiceAccountToken volume projection so pods receive a service account token requested from the TokenRequest API, distributed as a volume instead of long-lived secrets. The KEP is recorded as replaced by KEP-1205 Bound Service Account Tokens; status is replaced.
output.rationale: The KEP addressed the security and scalability problems of storing service account tokens as secrets by delivering node-requested tokens through a projected volume. The sources state that the KEP was closed because it was replaced by issue #542 (the Bound Service Account Tokens enhancement) and that the replacement KEP was merged. Reviewers also asked for a note linking the README to the replacing work.
output.outcome_reason: The sources say it was replaced by KEP-1205 Bound Service Account Tokens (referenced as issue #542), and the status history records replacement from 2021-05-07. They do not give a detailed technical reason beyond that the replacement KEP was merged.

alternatives.option: Implement all token injection as a flex volume or CSI plugin
alternatives.why_not: The readme says both flex volume and CSI are alpha and unlikely to graduate soon, and virtual kubelets may not be able to run flex volumes.

alternatives.option: Remove service accounts and service account tokens from core and use an external mechanism
alternatives.why_not: The readme says service account tokens are a fundamental part of the API, and other core features need service account integration, which would force all users to install an extension.

evidence.quote: Kubernetes should implement a ServiceAccountToken volume projection that maintains a service account token requested by the node from the TokenRequest API.
/close because it is replaced by https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/542 and the KEP is merged
probably worth adding a note/link in the README for this as well
